name: Symbolic MRD
description: A successor to Modular Relaxed Dependencies (MRD) and the first thin-air-free memory model to admit compiler optimisations that aggressively leverage alias analysis, an assumption of freedom from undefined behaviour, and the extrinsic choices of real implementations (e.g. over-alignment). Built on symbolic execution, it models dynamic memory — allocation, dereferencing, and reclamation — rather than only concrete locations, and exports a semantic-dependency relation that integrates with the C/C++ memory model, preserving the standard compilation mappings for atomics. It matches every test in the recently published ISO C/C++ semantic-dependency desiderata, and its tooling runs orders of magnitude faster than other executable thin-air-free semantics.

catSupport.note: Same event-structure/denotational shape as MRD, with symbolic addresses on top; no per-candidate-execution predicate to encode in cat.
